data.name: Message_LanguageRestartRequired
data.value: The new language will take effect after the application is restarted. Restart now?

data.name: Message_LanguageChangedToSystemDefault
data.value: Language reset to system default. Restart for the change to take effect?

data.name: Timeout_Tooltip
data.value: Maximum seconds to wait for the multiotp.exe child process. Applies to every action in this manager (except AD/LDAP queries, which always wait at least 30s). Increase this if you see spurious "timeout" failures on a SQL, LDAP or PrivacyIDEA backend.

data.name: Verify_Tooltip
data.value: Run the dry-run multiotp -verify command instead of the real authenticator. The OTP is checked against the time window but not consumed, so you can re-test the same code without burning the user's next login. Use this when troubleshooting "wrong OTP" reports.

data.name: DisablePin_Tooltip
data.value: Turn off the prefix-PIN prompt for this user so they only enter the OTP (lower security but easier to type). Only applies to login, not unlock.

data.name: Resync_Tooltip
data.value: Re-align the user's authenticator after clock drift. You will be asked for two consecutive OTP codes - the second one must be the immediate next code.

data.name: QrCode_Tooltip
data.value: Show the otpauth:// provisioning QR code for the selected user. The temporary image is deleted from disk right after it is loaded into the dialog - screenshot it now if you need to keep it.

data.name: RefreshTokens_Tooltip
data.value: Re-read the multiOTP hardware/software token inventory (-tokenslist). The token list panel below the users tab is informational only - this is the real token store.

data.name: TokensList_Tooltip
data.value: Inventory of every hardware/software token registered with multiOTP. Use the Assign/Remove buttons on the right to link a token to a user or unlink it. Delete removes the token from the store entirely.

data.name: AssignToken_Tooltip
data.value: Link the typed TOKEN ID to the typed USERNAME. The token must already exist in the token list above.

data.name: RemoveToken_Tooltip
data.value: Unlink the typed TOKEN ID from the typed USERNAME. The token remains in the store and can be assigned to someone else.

data.name: DeleteToken_Tooltip
data.value: Permanently remove the typed TOKEN ID from the multiOTP token store. Any user previously assigned to it loses access immediately.

data.name: LogonScope_Tooltip
data.value: Where the multiOTP credential provider requires a second factor. 'Local and remote' covers console + RDP; 'Remote desktop only' leaves the console on Windows password; 'Local only' disables 2FA on RDP; 'Disabled' turns the multiOTP login prompt off entirely (users will log in with their Windows password).

data.name: UnlockScope_Tooltip
data.value: Same as LOGON SCOPE but applies only to unlocking an already-signed-in workstation (the dialog you see when you press Ctrl+Alt+Del -> Lock). Independent of the logon setting.

data.name: LogonProviders_Tooltip
data.value: 'multiOTP only' means multiOTP intercepts the credential tile and the user must pass 2FA before Windows accepts the password. 'Other providers allowed' lets the built-in password provider still work, so users without an enrolled token can still sign in.

data.name: UnlockProviders_Tooltip
data.value: Same exclusivity choice as LOGON PROVIDERS, applied to the workstation-unlock prompt.

data.name: TwoStepHideOtp_Tooltip
data.value: When checked, the user types the OTP in the same field as the Windows password (single-step). When unchecked, Windows asks for the password first and then a separate OTP field (two-step). Single-step is friendlier but some screen-keyboard / kiosk setups need the two-step layout.

data.name: BackupRestore_Tooltip
data.value: Encrypted backup / restore of the entire multiOTP configuration: every user record, every token seed, AD/LDAP settings, server options, and the cache. The password is held in memory only and is required both for backup and for restore.

data.name: PurgeLock_Tooltip
data.value: Delete the multiOTP.lock folder, which is used to serialize authentication across servers. Run this only when no other multiOTP process is authenticating and you suspect stale lock files from a crash are blocking every login.

data.name: PurgeLdapCache_Tooltip
data.value: Drop the local LDAP user-info cache. The next AD/LDAP sync will fully repopulate it from the directory server. Use after changing LDAP filters or attribute mappings.

data.name: LdapCheck_Tooltip
data.value: Run multiotp -ldap-check to verify connectivity, credentials and search base against the configured AD/LDAP server. Read-only.

data.name: LdapUsersList_Tooltip
data.value: Run multiotp -ldap-users-list to enumerate the AD/LDAP users that match the configured filter. Read-only - nothing is written to multiOTP or to AD.

data.name: LdapSync_Tooltip
data.value: Run multiotp -ldap-users-sync. This is a write operation: it pushes multiOTP-side user attributes (email, display name, description, group) back into AD on matching accounts, and pulls missing users in. Run LDAP CHECK first if anything looks wrong.

data.name: ClearLog_Tooltip
data.value: Permanently delete the multiOTP debug log. The log may be needed for support or auditing - confirm before clearing.

data.name: ErrorCodes_Tooltip
data.value: Print the full multiOTP exit-code dictionary (-error-codes). Useful when the status bar shows a numeric code you do not recognise.

data.name: VersionBtn_Tooltip
data.value: Print the version of the bundled multiotp.exe (and the manager).
